title: Mintlify Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs and Overages
summary: Mintlify pricing ranges from free to $450/month for Pro billed annually. Compare all plans and see how monthly billing adds $1,080 yearly to your costs.
body_markdown:
## Mintlify pricing today: every plan, price and limit


Mintlify pricing is the set of tiered subscription plans through which Mintlify charges for its hosted documentation platform, with each plan's price and limits on seats, AI usage and features determining when a team must upgrade.


### The plan table, checked 4 November 2026


If your docs budget was approved on an older quote, it's probably wrong. Pro launched at[$150 a month](https://www.mintlify.com/pricing) . The Growth plan ended at $250, Pro then sat at $300, and it now sits at $450.


**That's a threefold rise from launch** , so any spreadsheet built on the early number understates the bill by $300 a month.


As of 4 November 2026, two tiers have figures I can confirm. Pro is $450 a month billed annually or $540 billed monthly, so month-to-month costs $90 more.


Nobody can tell you the Enterprise price from the page. It's "Contact us", which means it's unpriced and you only learn the figure after a sales call. Read this as a price check, then use the sections below to find where the limits sit.


Because Enterprise has no public price, you can't budget for it from the page alone. Assume a quote conversation and a timeline to match.


### What counts as a seat on each plan


You will undercount seats, because the people who edit docs are rarely the people you first count. Engineers, a technical writer, a support lead fixing one broken page: each may need an editor login.


> You will undercount seats, because the people who edit docs are rarely the people you first count.


Count every person who will touch the content in a quarter, not just the owner. Check how the pricing page defines an editor before you sign, because that definition sets how fast the plan outgrows you.


### Which Mintlify plan limit forces an upgrade


Whichever line you hit first forces the upgrade: editor seats, AI usage, or a feature locked to a higher tier. The sticker price is the smaller part of the decision.


Price your actual workload against each of those three before choosing. Ask how many editors you have, how often your team will use the AI features, and whether any must-have feature sits above Pro.


If your docs team also runs automations, those have their own meters, so compare each tool against your workload, not against each other's headline price.
